name: __WORKER_NAME__
//workers_dev: Terraform owns this Worker's hostname, so Wrangler must not attach one. Left true, Wrangler refuses to deploy into an account with no workers.dev subdomain registered -- and registering one would publish the webhook at a second, unmanaged URL.

r2_buckets.//: Deleted from and never written to: a draft cancelled after the media pipeline uploaded its derivatives leaves files nothing references, and the author has just declined them. Everything in this bucket is written by GitHub Actions, after sanitisation.

//triggers: Drives the scheduled handler in src/index.ts, which reports drafts stranded in `processing` by a run that never came back. Here rather than in Terraform on purpose: the schedule and the handler it invokes are one change, and deploy-worker runs on every push to worker/** while terraform-apply does not -- a cron owned by Terraform would silently not exist on a Worker deployed without an apply. Terraform still owns the custom domain, because that is a hostname in a zone rather than a property of the script.
//triggers.cadence: Every quarter of an hour, against a stranded-after threshold of 30 minutes (drafts/sweep.ts): a stranded draft is reported 30 to 45 minutes after dispatch. Tightening this without lowering the threshold buys nothing but invocations.
